title: Session Tombstone & Rollback Protocol — notes
content:
Purpose: quick brain dump for a lightweight session "tombstone" + rollback protocol for the client-side session offload / server reclaim flow. Goal is low-complexity, consistent rehydration and safe resource reclamation across host failures and multi-client handoffs.

Context / motivation:
- Current offload (epochal-session-bundle-format) sketches assume atomic put/get semantics, but we need a way to mark sessions as invalidated (tombstoned) and allow clients and servers to coordinate a rollback when mid-session state is lost or corrupted.
- Avoid long-lived locks and heavy consensus for common-case: most sessions are short-lived and either fully resumed or dropped. We want:
  * fast resume for normal cases (no extra coord)
  * safe quick reclaim when host goes away
  * deterministic client-visible rollback when partial state/drift is detected

Key ideas (high-level):
1) Session versioning + ephemeral receipts: every session bundle has (tenant, session_id, epoch, generation, checksum). When a session is offloaded, server writes a tombstone-free bundle and signs a short-lived receipt (TTL ~ 10m). Receipt maps to a recovery hint: preferred host or replica set id.
2) Conditional tombstone marker: if server decides to evacuate capacity / decommission, it writes a tombstone with (session_id, generation, reason, replaced_by?) and an optional rollback_manifest pointer. Tombstone is authoritative for that generation.
3) Client-visible rollback: when client rehydrates and sees tombstone with higher generation, client attempts to re-run model-startup sequence up to rollback point using rollback_manifest (a minimal diff or precomputed checkpoint). If rollback_manifest missing, client falls back to sanitized-start (drop ephemeral context) and emits a telemetry event.

API sketches (HTTP-friendly shapes):
- POST /sessions/offload
  Request JSON: {"tenant": "str", "session_id": "str", "bundle": "base64", "epoch": int, "generation": int, "checksum": "hex", "pref_replica": "replica-id?"}
  Response: {"receipt": "short-opaque", "expires_at": "iso-timestamp", "recovery_hint": "replica-id|region"}

- POST /sessions/tombstone
  Request JSON: {"tenant": "str", "session_id": "str", "generation": int, "reason": "str", "rollback_manifest_ref": "ref-or-url-or-empty"}
  Response: {"ok": true, "tombstone_id": "uuid", "applied_at": "iso-ts"}

- GET /sessions/rehydrate?tenant=...&session_id=...&receipt=...
  Response success: {"bundle": "base64", "generation": int, "receipt_verified": true}
  Response tombstoned: {"tombstoned": true, "generation": int, "rollback_manifest_ref": "url|null", "advice": "drop|replay|contact-operator"}

Operational notes / invariants:
- Tombstone applies to generation number; servers must honor highest-seen generation to avoid ABA. (i.e., if a newer generation offload exists, tombstone for older generation is no-op).
- Receipts are short-lived auth tokens. They do not override tombstone semantics — if a tombstone is issued after a receipt, rehydrate will return tombstone unless the tombstone was rolled back (rare).
- Rollback_manifest: ideally small, deterministic replay script (list of prompt deltas + KV ops) rather than full snapshot; reduces storage and speeds rollback. Manifest has a checksum; rehydrating client must verify.
- Telemetry: emit events for: receipt-miss, tombstone-detected, rollback-success, rollback-fallback, rehydrate-failure. Add counters per-tenant and per-route to detect noisy tenants.

ASCII diagram (sequence):
Client           OffloadHost            ArchiveStore           RecoveryHost
  |                 |                       |                     |
  |--POST offload-->|                       |                     |
  |<--receipt--------|                       |                     |
  |                 (later)                  |                     |
  |--GET rehydrate->|--(detect tombstone)-->+write tombstone+     |
  |                 |                       |   (tombstone)       |
  |                 |<--response tombstoned--|                     |
  |--follow rollback (fetch manifest)----->|--fetch manifest---->|
  |--local replay->|                       |                     |
  |--if fallback, start fresh context------>                      |

Edge cases / unresolved questions (TODO):
- Simultaneous offload and tombstone: race where an offload for gen=N completes while tombstone for gen=N-1 is applied — ok as long as rules treat tombstone scoped to generation only. Need to detect duplicate writes.
- How to GC tombstones? If tombstone has TTL longer than receipts, a client could keep trying. Plan: tombstones are kept for min(T_garbage_collect, tenant_retention) plus index for quick filter. Also tombstone compaction: keep only last 1 per session id.
- Cross-tenant replay safety: rollback_manifest must be scoped and signed for tenant to avoid cross-tenant leakage. Enforce server-side ACL checks.
- What if rollback_manifest is larger than bundle? then maybe prefer full snapshot; metric threshold to choose manifest vs snapshot at offload time.

Implementation sketch (pseudocode):
- Offload path (server):
  1) compute bundle, generation = last_generation + 1
  2) write bundle to archiveStore under key (tenant/session/generation) atomically
  3) emit receipt mapping to key with TTL

- Tombstone path (operator / automated):
  1) write tombstone record: {session_id, generation=g, reason, manifest_ref or null, created_at}
  2) increment tombstone-index(session_id -> latest_gen)
  3) notify watchers (optional)

- Rehydrate path (client):
  1) call GET /rehydrate with receipt (if present)
  2) server checks latest tombstone; if tombstoned and tombstone.g >= requested.g -> return tombstone payload
  3) if manifest_ref present: server returns manifest ref; client fetches manifest and runs deterministic rollback sequence; if success -> resume; else -> fallback to fresh-context and emit failure metric

Failure modes and safety nets:
- Incomplete manifest replay -> client should fail safe to fresh context and log audit/telemetry. Provide operator manual reclaim flow to re-run replay on server side.
- Archive inconsistency -> server must verify bundle checksum on rehydrate. If mismatch, tombstone+alert.

Metrics to capture (minimum):
- offload_success, offload_latency_ms
- receipt_verify_success, receipt_verify_failure
- rehydrate_success, rehydrate_tombstoned, rehydrate_missing_bundle
- rollback_manifest_fetch_failures, rollback_manifest_apply_failures
- tombstone_write_ops, tombstone_gc_ops

Open design decisions (short list):
- TTLs: receipt TTL ~ 5–15 minutes; tombstone retention configurable per-tenant (default 7d?)
- Manifest format: replay-script vs delta-ops vs full-checkpoint. Starting point: small json-lines replay script + optional compressed blob.
- Consistency model: eventual for archive store, but tombstones must be applied with linearizable writes to index (or monotonic generation checks) to avoid lost-applies. Explore using a lightweight coordinator (etcd) for index writes vs store-based compare-and-set.

Next steps / action items for me:
- Prototype minimal manifest schema (json-lines) and small parser to exercise a rollback sequence against local polyglot runner.
- Add lightweight tombstone index using existing meta-store (see github PR link above) and write simple GC job.
- Sketch UX for client-side library: rehydrate() should be ergonomic: return enum {RESUMED, ROLLED_BACK, FRESH_START} plus telemetry payload.

Notes to self:
- Keep protocol minimal: prefer clear failure modes over magical auto-repair.
- Lean on telemetry to decide whether manifests are worth the complexity: if rollbacks < 0.1% maybe we default to fresh start and simpler offload.

References / quick links (for later copy/paste):
- existing bundle proto: github.com/redwood-inference/bundles/blob/main/bundle.proto
- offload GC job: JIRA-RT-302
- team thread: slack #sess-offload (search "tombstone")

-- end of dump --
